channel.title: Financial Regulation Hub · Exchanges
channel.description: New and amended rules from National Stock Exchange and BSE, as covered by the Financial Regulation Hub.

item.title: Exchanges: Further issues: one lead exchange handles queries for both NSE and BSE
item.description:
Exchanges · Exchange circular · NSE/CML/2026/22

Effective 2026-11-01.

Who it covers: Listed companies applying for in-principle approval of a further issue of shares.

  • Applications are still filed with every exchange, but the exchanges assign a lead exchange in turn.
  • The other exchange routes its queries through the lead exchange; the company answers only the lead exchange.
  • Applies to applications filed on or after 01-11-2026.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: RFQ trades in corporate bonds settle on T+0 until 5 p.m.
item.description:
Exchanges · Exchange circular · NSE/DS/76973; BSE notice 20261019-21

Effective 2026-10-19.

Who it covers: Participants on the NSE and BSE RFQ platforms.

  • RFQ trading hours for T+0 settlement extended to 5 p.m. (NSE from 19-10-2026; BSE from 21-10-2026).
  • Participants must confirm their entity type every half-year to keep platform access.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: Newly debt-listed entities must list all later NCDs
item.description:
Exchanges · SEBI regulation · SEBI/LAD-DOP/2026/329 (LODR Third Amendment)

Effective 2026-10-14.

Who it covers: Entities whose non-convertible debt securities are listed on or after 14-10-2026.

  • Reg 62A(1) substituted: an entity whose NCDs are listed on or after the amendment's Gazette publication (14-10-2026) must list all non-convertible debt securities it issues after that listing.
  • Reg 62A(2) and (3) omitted.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: Credit Risk-o-Meter on debt offer documents and bond platforms
item.description:
Exchanges · Exchange circular · NSE circular of 08-10-2026; BSE notice 20261008-23

Effective 2026-11-21.

Who it covers: Debt issuers, arrangers and online bond platform providers.

  • Offer documents, placement memoranda, advertisements and online bond platforms must show a Credit Risk-o-Meter.
  • The rating agency, the rating and, for unsecured debt, the word 'unsecured' in bold red appear below it.
  • In force 45 days after 07-10-2026.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: Rs 10,000 NCDs: some regulated, listed issuers need no merchant banker
item.description:
Exchanges · Exchange circular · NSE/CML/D/2026/06; BSE notice 20261008-22

Effective 2026-10-07.

Who it covers: Issuers regulated by SEBI, RBI, IRDAI or PFRDA, including NBFCs and HFCs.

  • For private placements at Rs 10,000 face value, no merchant banker is needed if the issuer is regulated by SEBI, RBI, IRDAI or PFRDA; has been listed for a year with no pending LODR fines; has had no default in the last three financial years and the current year (auditor's certificate); issues senior debt secured on its own identifiable assets; and is rated AA- or above on the placement date.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: New caps on ISINs for privately placed debt
item.description:
Exchanges · Exchange circular · NSE/CML/D/2026/05; BSE notice 20261008-21

Effective 2026-10-07.

Who it covers: Issuers of privately placed debt securities and their arrangers.

  • Up to 17 ISINs may mature in a financial year: 12 for plain vanilla debt and 5 for structured, market-linked, floating rate, zero coupon and Tier II bonds, plus 6 for s. 54EC bonds.
  • Outstanding floating rate, zero coupon and Tier II ISINs issued before the circular are grandfathered.
  • One more plain vanilla ISIN for each Rs 3,000 crore once the amount maturing in the year reaches Rs 15,000 crore.
  • Government-serviced (EBR) bonds and ESG debt securities are outside the count.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: Revised window for tri-party repo auctions in corporate bonds
item.description:
Exchanges · Exchange circular · NSE/DS/76400

Effective 2026-09-18.

Who it covers: Participants in tri-party repo in corporate bonds.

  • Repo auctions run between 3.30 p.m. and 4 p.m. from 18-09-2026.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: BSE's list of companies with high promoter pledge
item.description:
Exchanges · Exchange notice · BSE notice 20260902-39

Effective 2026-09-07.

Who it covers: Listed companies on the list, their promoters, and lenders holding pledges.

  • Listed securities attract a minimum 35% margin on all open and new positions in the equity and derivatives segments.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: Changes to the framework for online bond platforms
item.description:
Exchanges · Exchange circular · NSE/COMP/75793; BSE notice 20260817-28

Effective 2026-08-14.

Who it covers: Online bond platform providers and stock brokers.

  • SEBI modified the OBPP framework for ease of doing business; OBPPs also show the Credit Risk-o-Meter from 21-11-2026.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: One filing reaches both NSE and BSE
item.description:
Exchanges · Exchange circular · NSE/CML/2026/17; BSE notice 20260619-11

Effective 2026-06-20.

Who it covers: Listed entities filing Regulation 30 disclosures.

  • A filing through the common system counts for both exchanges.
  • For covered events the PDF counts as compliance, with the XBRL filing to follow within 24 hours.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: FAQs on the quarterly Integrated Filing (Governance)
item.description:
Exchanges · Exchange circular · NSE/CML/2026/16; BSE notice 20260612-13

Effective 2026-06-12.

Who it covers: Equity-listed entities.

  • Clarifies scope and timing: file within 30 days of each quarter end; newly listed entities start with the first quarter ending after listing.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: Lock-in of pledged shares
item.description:
Exchanges · Exchange circular · NSE/CML/2026/07

Effective 2026-04-08.

Who it covers: Issuers with locked-in pledged shares, and lenders or pledgees.

  • Issuers follow the depositories' framework for locked-in pledged shares: suitable provisions in the articles, intimation to lenders and disclosure in the offer document.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: MPS fines paused for due dates from April to September 2026
item.description:
Exchanges · Exchange circular · NSE/CML/2026/06; BSE notice 20260409-3

Effective 2026-04-07.

Who it covers: Listed companies whose minimum public shareholding due date falls in the window.

  • For entities whose MPS due date falls between 01-04-2026 and 30-09-2026: no penal action for non-compliance during that window, and actions already taken against them from 01-04-2026 are withdrawn.
  • Entities whose due date fell earlier get no relief.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: NSE guidelines for the Liquidity Window Facility
item.description:
Exchanges · Exchange circular · NSE/DS/72742

Effective 2026-02-11.

Who it covers: Debt issuers offering a liquidity window to retail investors, and those investors.

  • Optional, per ISIN at issue: exercisable only after one year, at least 10% of the issue, three-working-day windows, payout no more than 100 basis points below valuation plus accrued interest.
  • Notice of each window at least 3 working days before; application at least 2 working days before.
  • Put price from a rating agency's valuation uploaded by 6 p.m. on T-1.
  • Settlement on T+4 without settlement guarantee; disclosures within three working days after the window.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: NCS amendment: incentives for retail, senior citizens and others
item.description:
Exchanges · SEBI regulation · SEBI/LAD-NRO/GN/2026/296

Effective 2026-01-20.

Who it covers: Issuers of non-convertible securities.

  • Issuers may offer extra interest or a discount to senior citizens, women, serving and retired defence personnel, widows and widowers of defence personnel, retail investors and other specified categories.
  • Only the initial allottee gets it; it does not pass on transfer or transmission.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: High value debt listed entity threshold raised to Rs 5,000 crore
item.description:
Exchanges · SEBI regulation · SEBI/NRO-GN/2026/295

Effective 2026-01-20.

Who it covers: Debt-only listed entities, including NBFCs and HFCs.

  • The reg 15(1A) threshold for the corporate governance provisions that apply to high value debt listed entities rose from Rs 1,000 crore to Rs 5,000 crore of listed non-convertible debt securities.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: Rs 10,000 debt securities can now be zero coupon
item.description:
Exchanges · Exchange circular · NSE/CML/2025/14; BSE notice 20251222-26

Effective 2025-12-18.

Who it covers: Issuers privately placing debt with a face value of Rs 10,000.

  • Zero coupon instruments allowed at the Rs 10,000 face value, for placements listed from 18-12-2025.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: Trustees can use the Recovery Expense Fund without holders' prior consent
item.description:
Exchanges · Exchange circular · NSE/CML/2025/12; BSE notice 20251127-66

Effective 2025-11-25.

Who it covers: Debt issuers, debenture trustees and debenture holders.

  • After a default, trustees may draw REF for listed enforcement purposes without holders' prior approval.
  • The exchange releases REF within five working days of the trustee's intimation.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: Fixed timelines for information issuers send to debenture trustees
item.description:
Exchanges · Exchange circular · BSE notice 20251127-64

Effective 2025-12-31.

Who it covers: Issuers of secured listed debt and their trustees.

  • Quarterly security cover and related statements within 60 days of quarter end (75 days for the last quarter).
  • Half-yearly guarantor net worth and annual guarantor financials within 60 days; three-yearly valuation and title search reports.
  • Applies from the quarter ended 31-12-2025.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: Regulation 50 intimations only in XBRL
item.description:
Exchanges · Exchange circular · NSE/CML/2025/09; BSE notice 20251121-72

Effective 2025-12-01.

Who it covers: Entities with listed non-convertible securities.

  • From 01-12-2025, prior intimations under reg 50 go only in XBRL; any other mode counts as non-submission.

Official source
